name: SkyWest, Inc.
tagline: Regional airline operator providing scheduled passenger service under code-share agreements
hero_kpi_rationale: Pilier financier représentant 84,3% des revenus d'exploitation, généré par les accords de capacité avec les grandes compagnies aériennes partenaires

kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from capacity purchase agreements with major airline partners
kpis.signal: Significant increase driven by higher block hours and increased aircraft utilization due to improved captain availability
kpis.description: Revenue generated from capacity purchase agreements where major airline partners pay fixed rates based on completed flights, flight time and aircraft under contract
kpis._validation: Corrected value from 3.5B to 2591M (actual capacity purchase revenue from 10-K); corrected unit from Mds $ to M $; corrected yoy to +10.8% (matches 10-K); updated tagline to English; improved rationale in French

kpis.explanation: Revenue from prorate agreements and on-demand charter services (SWC)
kpis.signal: Strong growth from higher passenger numbers and increased prorate/charter flights; company bears operating costs and shares passenger revenues
kpis.description: Revenue from agreements where company shares passenger fares with major airline partners and controls scheduling/pricing on certain routes; includes on-demand charter revenue
kpis._validation: Corrected value from 0.6B to 607M (actual prorate and SWC revenue from 10-K); corrected unit from Mds $ to M $; renamed to 'Prorate and Charter Revenue' for accuracy; updated tagline to English

kpis.explanation: Total number of aircraft in the operating fleet
kpis.signal: Slight net increase reflecting fleet modernization with E175 additions and older CRJ aircraft removals
kpis.description: Total number of aircraft in fleet including scheduled service, leased to third parties, and spare aircraft supporting code-share agreements
kpis._validation: Corrected yoy from -1.0% to +1.1% (630 aircraft in 2024 vs 637 in 2025); updated name_en to 'Total Fleet Aircraft'; updated tagline to English; corrected is_generic from true to false

stories_kpis.Signal: Significant growth reflecting strategic fleet modernization and replacement of older aircraft with newer, more efficient E175s
stories_kpis.Description: Number of E175 regional jet aircraft (manufactured by Embraer) in scheduled service or under contract, representing primary modernization focus
stories_kpis._validation: Corrected yoy from +3.0% to +3.1% (262 in 2024 vs 270 in 2025 = 8/262 = 3.05%); updated Name_en to 'E175 Aircraft in Service'; updated Signal to English and emphasize strategic fleet modernization

stories_kpis._validation: Corrected yoy from 'stable' to '0.0%'; updated Name_en to 'CRJ900 Aircraft in Service'; corrected Signal to English

ai_positioning.summary: SkyWest does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing

risks.title: Dependence on Code-Share Agreements with Major Airline Partners
risks.score_rationale: Code-share agreements represent the core business model, with capacity purchase revenue alone representing 84.3% of flying agreement revenues. Contract termination or renegotiation could materially impact revenue stability and operations (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: The company is heavily dependent on long-term code-share agreements with United, Delta, American and Alaska Airlines. Any termination, non-renewal or adverse renegotiation of these agreements would have significant negative impact on operations and profitability

risks.title: Volatility in Maintenance and Fuel Costs
risks.score_rationale: Operating expenses increased 13.4% YoY while revenue grew 15.0%, with capacity purchase agreements providing fuel reimbursement but prorate agreements exposing company to fuel price volatility. Fleet age and increased utilization drive maintenance pressures (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Rising fuel and maintenance costs pose profitability risks, particularly on prorate routes where company bears operating costs. Increased aircraft utilization and fleet mix transition add maintenance complexity and potential cost surprises

risks.title: Fleet Modernization Transition and Integration Risks
risks.score_rationale: Company undergoing significant fleet changes with E175 additions (8 aircraft in 2025, 9-10 additional planned for 2026) and CRJ aircraft phase-outs. Delivery delays, integration challenges and removal of older high-maintenance aircraft create operational risks (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Ongoing fleet modernization involves adding new E175 aircraft and removing older CRJ200 and CRJ700 aircraft. Risks include aircraft delivery delays, pilot training requirements, and operational disruption during transition

risks.title: Labor Availability and Pilot Shortage Constraints
risks.score_rationale: Captain availability was a binding constraint in 2024 but less restrictive in 2025, allowing 14.7% increase in block hours. However, future growth remains dependent on pilot labor availability. Salary pressures evident in 6.5% increase in personnel costs (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Adequate captain availability enabled increased utilization in 2025, but potential pilot shortages could limit growth. Rising pilot compensation and industry-wide labor market tightness create ongoing cost pressures and operational constraints

risks.title: Prorate Agreement Revenue Volatility and Operating Cost Exposure
risks.score_rationale: Prorate revenue grew 33.5% to $607M (15.7% of flying agreement revenue), but exposes company to passenger traffic fluctuations, fuel price volatility, and airport cost variations while bearing full operating costs (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Growing reliance on prorate agreements (now 15.7% of flying agreement revenue) increases exposure to passenger demand volatility and fuel/cost inflation. Unlike capacity purchase agreements, prorate routes require company to absorb cost overruns

risks.title: Passenger Load Factor Compression
risks.score_rationale: Passenger load factor declined from 82.8% in 2024 to 81.5% in 2025 (1.3 percentage point decline) despite 8.7% passenger growth, indicating potential pricing pressure or demand softness that could impact prorate revenue quality (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Declining load factor despite passenger growth suggests capacity additions outpaced demand growth or pricing pressure. This metric warrants monitoring for prorate route profitability and revenue yield
